extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users, mathematicians, technical authors, and programmers seeking a language for high-quality vector graphics and technical figures
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Asymptote vector graphics language: its features, design goals, supported outputs, implementation details, and example usage for producing technical and mathematical figures (including 3D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Output formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote typesets labels and equations with LaTeX, producing high-quality PostScript, PDF, SVG, or 3D PRC output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Asymptote when you need publication-quality vector output; the language can produce 2D formats (PostScript, PDF, SVG) and a 3D PRC format. The article's example shows generating a PDF from Asymptote source (outformat = "pdf" and size directives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with LaTeX (typesetting labels and equations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote typesets labels and equations with LaTeX, allowing mathematical notation to match TeX/LaTeX documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels in figures can use TeX math markup (e.g. Label("$x$", ...)). This makes Asymptote suitable for figures that must integrate seamlessly with LaTeX-typed text and equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax and language paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote has a C-like syntax and is imperative and typesetting-oriented; it was inspired by MetaPost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmers familiar with C-like languages will find the syntax familiar. The language is designed for describing graphics programmatically rather than purely declaratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematically oriented / coordinate-based framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a natural coordinate-based framework for technical drawing; is mathematically oriented (e.g. rotation of vectors by complex multiplication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asymptote's primitives are designed for mathematical reasoning about figures (vectors, rotations, paths), making it appropriate for technical diagrams in mathematics and related fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of size constraints (simplex method and deferred drawing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses the simplex method and deferred drawing to solve overall size constraint issues between fixed-sized objects (labels and arrowheads) and objects that should scale with figure size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred drawing and constraint solving let Asymptote reconcile elements that must remain fixed-size (like labels) with scalable graphical objects, improving layout correctness without manual adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D generalization and lifting TeX to 3D
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote fully generalizes MetaPost path construction algorithms to three dimensions and claims to lift TeX into three dimensions, enabling 3D vector file output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asymptote can be used as a 3D vector file format; consult the referenced papers for details on the 3D Bézier interpolation and examples of 3D usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance model / compilation to virtual machine
rubrics_metrics.description: Compiles commands into virtual machine code for speed without sacrificing portability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asymptote source is compiled into bytecode for a VM which improves runtime performance while remaining cross-platform; this matters for complex or programmatically generated graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level extensibility (graphics commands implemented in-language)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level graphics commands are implemented in the Asymptote language itself, allowing them to be easily tailored to specific applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can extend or modify provided high-level routines in Asymptote source to customize behavior for domain-specific drawing tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical front-end (xasy.py) for beginner users
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote has a graphical interface coded in Python (xasy.py, using the Tk widget set) that lets inexperienced users draw objects and save them as .asy source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use xasy.py to prototype or create drawings interactively, then inspect or hand-edit the generated .asy source for refinement or automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote runs on all major platforms (Unix, Mac OS, Microsoft Windows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Asymptote when you need portability across common operating systems; binaries and source are available for multiple platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: License / free software status
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote is free software available under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LGPL license affects how Asymptote can be redistributed or embedded; projects requiring permissive licenses may need to consider compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application domain: technical and mathematical figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote is a language for typesetting mathematical figures, analogous to how TeX/LaTeX typeset equations; it's intended for technical drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The included Heaviside function example demonstrates creating mathematical plots and annotated axes; use Asymptote for precise, programmatic technical diagrams rather than freehand illustration tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: MetaPost relationship and path-construction compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote is inspired by MetaPost and generalizes MetaPost path construction algorithms (including Bézier interpolation) to higher dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users familiar with MetaPost can leverage similar concepts in Asymptote, with additional 3D capabilities; the article cites papers on the 3D generalization and Bézier regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example-driven usage (code example for Heaviside function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article includes a concrete Asymptote source example that draws a graph of the Heaviside function, showing imports, output format, drawing commands, axes, ticks, labels, and fill/draw primitives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the example to learn program structure (imports, outformat, size, draw/fill, axis/label commands). It demonstrates practical idioms such as splitting piecewise plots, styling lines, dashed lines, filled/unfilled circles, and axis ticks/labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability with other tools and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Related/see-also tools include GeoGebra (with Asymptote export), PSTricks, TikZ, PyX; Asymptote occupies a position among vector graphics and markup languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing a toolkit, compare Asymptote against alternatives (TikZ/PGF, PSTricks) for integration with existing workflows, feature sets (2D vs 3D), and user familiarity.
